In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

selective venous sampling from either the cavernous sinouses or the inferior petrosals sinuses is an accurate method of localizing pituitary ACTH production in patients with ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome.

selective CS sampling with CRH stimulation has not proven itself to be superior to IPS sampling with CRH in the evaluation of patients with ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome, although it may have some value in lateralization.
the use of CRH stimulation during venous sampling is superior to the use of CS sampling for the differential diagnosis and lateralization of ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome.

the CS is not a more sensitive or reliable site for venous sampling than the IPS.
CS sampling is inferior to IPS sampling for the diagnosis and lateralization of ACTH-dependent Cushing's syndrome.

CS sampling without CRh stimulation is not recommended.
